name: Northeast Face
text: [detailed_rack] Standard rack with some long slings, since the line wanders, plus an ice axe.

name: Northwest Chute
text: [approach] From the lake go up gravel, talus and grass to Tower Pass, where the peak comes into view, cross the basin beyond, and climb slabs beside a lingering snow patch to the northwest ridge.

name: Northwest Couloir
text: [overview] Take the main gully to the narrows, where a 45 degree snow section runs between Tom's Wart and the face walls.

name: Ok Balto, hike!
text: [overview] The dihedral on the back side of the neighboring route, with glacier-polished gray rock on the part of the corner that faces left.

name: Planaria
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.

name: Plum Line
text: [approach] Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest;
[approach] snow can linger there into summer.

name: Power House Couloir
text: [overview] A lengthy mixed couloir of snow, rock and ice.
[detailed_rack] Ice tools, crampons and a rock rack.

name: Inconceivable
text: [overview] Mostly moderate snow with the odd rock step;
[overview] P1: a rock step 15' high may interrupt the lower snow, but heavy snowfall buries it and the pitch starts at the first rock band above.
[overview] P3: take the obvious weakness leftward to a small roof, which is bypassed on its right side, then an offwidth/chimney, steep, leads to the snowfield above;
[overview] P4: long snow with a short rock step ends at a chimney capped by a chockstone.
[overview] P5: torque in thin cracks right of the chimney, then mantle onto the snow gully.
[overview] P6: easy snow to the summit.
[approach] Snow over the talus makes it easier in winter and spring, and skis can be used.
[approach] The route is the only other full-length snow couloir left of the central couloir that splits the face.
[descent_text] Head southeast over moderate snow, then retrace the approach.

name: Rocky Canyon
text: [description] The trail can be hard to follow where snow lingers.

name: Quickly Without Asking (Tallac Headwall Direct)
text: [overview] Snow can move the start.
[what_to_bring] ice axes and perhaps crampons — getting to the wall base

name: North Gully
text: [overview] Alternatively, sidle west at the top of the snow for a Class 2 scramble to that plateau.
[overview] Staying east of the north face means trees and gentler slope, but less chance to self-arrest.
[overview] The true line goes west in a steeper chute holding consolidated snow into early summer.

name: North Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] pickets may suit winter and spring.
[approach] Start at Lake Wit-So-Nah-Pah and walk up to Constance Lake, then climb a moraine to the glacier at the foot of the couloir.

name: Crescent Moon Couloir
text: [overview] A short couloir of about 600 feet on snow at 40-50 degrees, with a fairly constant angle.
[overview] Difficulty is moderate and varies with snow conditions.

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] Snow cover matters: without it the loose rock band is likely unsafe.
[detailed_rack] If roping up, a few pickets can help manage the rope on the pitched section.

name: Saint's Way (AKA Y-Couloir)
text: [overview] Snow and rock of moderate difficulty, plus two brief cliff bands of 5th class, each with several ways through.

name: North Face Middle East Chute
text: [overview] After a lean snow season, scree fields cover the upper part.
[overview] Skiing or glissading down works when conditions are good.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] Early spring in a heavy snow year is the best time.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe.

name: Sierra Slam
text: [approach] Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest;
[approach] snow can linger there into summer.

name: Sky Pilot
text: [overview] From the snowfield, scramble left to a belay under the corner of the buttress route.

name: Stand Out Memory
text: [overview] A long, obvious runnel of snow and ice cutting through crumbly volcanic stone, found on the highway's south side where the Deadman curves sit, near 9000 elevation.
[approach] Park at the pullout skiers use for the snow bridge, cross the creek where it is safe, and skin, ski or hike up to the first tier.
[approach] If the first tier has no snow, a trail to the east (used for Blue Canyon) gives access from the side.

name: South Face
text: [detailed_rack] Small alpine rack of the usual kind, plus an ice axe in season.

name: South Lake Peaks Traverse
text: [overview] Best in summer without snow, though the last chute may hold some.

[overview] Order: Hurd Peak NE Arete, Peak 12,192' NE Ridge (class 2-3 down, 3rd then 4th up), Trapezoid Peak North Ridge, the crest to Mt Johnson, then its NW Ridge to Treasure Col and down the chute, snow or loose gully by season.
[detailed_rack] a compact ice axe can be useful.

name: South Ridge
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe — may be needed, depending on snowpack

name: Southeast Face
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — the couloir

name: Southeast Face
text: [approach] Expect snow cover on the stretch between Iceberg Lake and the foot of the route.

name: Southeast Face (aka the Waterfall Route)
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe — if the chute or descent holds snow

name: Northeast Couloir
text: [overview] The bergschrund can be large, and pitch 1 beyond it is an ice smear, vertical in places, over a bulge.
[overview] A snowfield above ranges from deep facets to hard neve.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons

name: Angels and Demons
text: [approach] The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake.

name: Friends
text: [approach] The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake.

name: Spring Roll
text: [approach] The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake.

name: St Jeans Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] Essentials: crampons, an ice axe and a helmet.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — required

name: Piper at the Gates of Dawn
text: [overview] Cracks plus a pair of roofs gain the slab's top, then easy ground by a snowfield and a traverse to a small arete bring you onto the summit ridge.

name: Sun Ribbon Arete
text: [approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
[approach] In the afternoon, climb to the base of the route in soft snow, which hardens by morning;
[approach] light aluminum crampons help on a car-to-car day early in the season.
[descent_text] then slog back down to the snowfield and your camp, or to the trail and the car.

name: Swiss Arete
text: [overview] the Glacier Notch couloir and then the L-Shaped Couloir lead to the ridge.
[detailed_rack] Alpine rack, carrying crampons and an ice-axe as well.
[descent] northwest ridge toward the neighbour peak, over to the north side at a spike, down a steep pitch and across a ledge to the notch, then the snowfield to the notch below

name: The Ice Gate
text: [descent_text] Two ways off: the snowfield below the fire lookout, which takes more effort, or the Altar Couloir, which is more technical.

name: Temple, Galey, Sill Traverse
text: [overview] From Galey, a ridge of class 2-3 drops to Glacier Notch;
[overview] the quickest way back to Palisade Glacier is Underhill Couloir (class 4, loose).
[approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
[descent_text] From its summit, descend the third-class ridge in the direction of Polemonium, then drop into the L-shaped couloir and Glacier Notch to reach the Palisade Glacier.

[descent_text] From the glacier, you can either go straight down to Second or Third Lake, which is more direct and best with snow, or follow the trail past Sam Mack Meadow to rejoin the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail.

name: The Apprentice
text: [approach] Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest;
[approach] snow can linger there into summer.

name: The Contender
text: [approach] Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest;
[approach] snow can linger there into summer.

name: The Mountaineer's Route
text: [descent_text] Early in the season, or after storms, snow and ice can stay in the upper gully into summer, so carry an axe and crampons, wear a helmet against rockfall, and do not glissade the upper gully, where hidden ice can send you out of control.

name: The Speed of Life
text: [overview] From the dam, cross over and hike a steep, loose hillside to the bottom-most tongue of the rock, often guarded by an ice or snow patch;

name: Southeast Slope from Birch Lake
text: [description] Follow the Birch Creek trail to Birch Lake, climb the steep ramp west of the lake to the crest, then ascend talus and snow to the summit.
[description] The ramp holds snow into summer and may need crampons.

name: The Watchtower | 1467
text: [approach] From the top of that ice, climb steep snow through the trees to the base of the first obstacle on the route.

name: Tokopah Falls
text: [approach] Where the trail stops, scramble down and cross snow bridges to get to the ice.

name: Thunder Mountain Northwest Slopes
text: [overview] Some winters lack enough snow, so watch weather and recent reports to pick a good day.
[overview] Climb Big Butch Wash to the east-northeast on moderate snow.
[overview] Falling boulders from steep couloirs overhead, and skiers or snowboarders descending the wash, are possible hazards.
[what_to_bring] crampons — depending on conditions.
[what_to_bring] ice axe — depending on conditions.
[what_to_bring] snowshoes — depending on conditions.

name: Thunderbolt to Sill Traverse
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe and/or crampons — the couloir descent.

name: Twilight Pillar
text: [overview] Gain the ridge right below where Firebird Ridge begins, traverse left beneath the major snowfield onto the lower part of the pillar, and follow the lower 5th class ridge to a ledge under the upper headwall.
[what_to_bring] ice axe — early in the season, for ice

name: U-Notch Couloir
text: [overview] A broad ice gully rising from the glacier into the wide gap beside the summit.
[overview] Getting over the bergschrund is the main difficulty.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — for the first part

name: Uncontrolled Burn
text: [approach] Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest;
[approach] snow can linger there into summer.

name: Northwest Shoulder
text: [detailed_rack] Only an ice axe, ski poles and crampons.

name: V-Notch Couloir
text: [overview] Fall is the best season, once the snowpack has shrunk to leftover ice.
[overview] The bergschrund crossing is the crux.

name: Venusian Blind
text: [overview] After crossing a horizontal ledge above the snowfield, the line wanders left over easy ground to a large slab, climbs a corner like an open book at its left side and stays along the slab's left margin up to the arete's nose.
[approach] Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake.
[approach] Venusian Blind shares its start with Moon Goddess Arete: a snow chute between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes leads to a snow and rock traverse to the base.
[approach] The snowfield is steep enough that crampons suit early season.
[descent_text] Below the pass, snow can be glissaded and rock and scree lead back to the lakes.

name: Why Ya Sufferin'?
text: [overview] P1 (50m): rock step to a snowfield, left to the hidden chute.
[overview] P2 (70m): steep 5.6 chimney, then the chute with mixed bits and a chockstone passed on the right, to Two Tree Snowfield.
[overview] P3 (65m): snow, a short mixed chockstone section, then Australia Snowfield.
[overview] P4 (70m): snow up-left, hard to protect.
[overview] P6 (35m): snow up-right and over a cornice.
[detailed_rack] Pickets or stakes are probably pointless in thin, loose snow.

name: Mt Whitney ski the Mountaineers Gully
text: [overview] Ascending may need ski crampons, with boot crampons and ice axe added when the Whitney summit is the goal;

name: Schneider Crest ski
text: [overview] Follow the Trail Crest approach to Consolation Lake, pass its NW side and work up along the slope's right-hand edge to Whitney Pass, then travel SE on the ridge, partly on its NE flank, to the snow summit;
[overview] Bring ski crampons, perhaps boot crampons.
